raw_evidence: In recent weeks, a spate of vandalism has seen up to 50 houses attacked in Salford and neighbouring areas of Greater Manchester Windows have been smashed, doors ripped from their hinges and walls daubed with graffiti opposing "HMOs" The term HMO is not widely known outside housing and planning circles. It stands for "House in Multiple Occupation" and refers to properties where three or more unrelated people live, usually with separate bedrooms but shared facilities such as kitchens and bathrooms While HMOs are often associated with students and young professionals, they can also provide accommodation for people leaving prison, those recovering from drug or alcohol problems, and refugees Police in Salford have said they believe that the recent spate of vandalism aimed at HMOs in the area has been "racially or religiously motivated" The term HMO was formalised in the Housing Act 1985. Before then, and for many years afterwards, such properties were more commonly known as bedsits or lodging houses
